statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across 58 checks and six representative paths.

page.notes: Server-rendered adult manhwa catalog and long-form image reader. Not covered: authenticated post-login states, account mutation, every title/chapter, payment (none observed), and exhaustive ad rotation; selected pages represent homepage, listing, detail, reader, search and error templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Light- and dark-preference screenshots are byte-identical (1,088,820 bytes) and both render the hard-coded dark theme; the page offers only a manual theme toggle.
The emulation probe matched reduced motion and found zero running animations; no auto-advance or essential motion was observed.

checkOutcomes.method: computed-style and focus probe under prefers-contrast: more plus Lighthouse
checkOutcomes.evidence: Controls and text remained visible; primary targets retained native focus outlines and Lighthouse accessibility/contrast audits passed.
The platform probe found View Transitions supported by the browser but no view-transition CSS usage; navigation is conventional abrupt document replacement.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon and applicability judgement across representative paths
checkOutcomes.evidence: No authored scroll-linked animation or parallax effect exists; there is no scroll event animation implementation to assess.
checkOutcomes.reason: No authored scroll-linked animation or parallax effect exists; there is no scroll event animation implementation to assess.

checkOutcomes.method: mobile screenshots and DOM/CSS interaction inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The chapter reader uses native vertical scrolling and fixed labelled Previous/Next controls; no custom pointermove gesture layer was found.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence review: evidence/chapter-mobile-layout.json, evidence/chapter-mobile.png, evidence/preferences-css.json
checkOutcomes.evidence: The chapter mobile layout is 69,269px tall, while the screenshot shows only a fixed chapter bar; the CSS probe found no scroll-state query or declarative progress treatment.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon and applicability judgement across representative paths
checkOutcomes.evidence: No tooltip or viewport-edge popover is part of the representative core paths; authentication uses modal dialogs instead.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip or viewport-edge popover is part of the representative core paths; authentication uses modal dialogs instead.

checkOutcomes.method: visual inspection of home, detail and chapter states
checkOutcomes.evidence: Active Home styling, clear Read First/Read Last actions, chapter title, back control and labelled Previous/Next controls preserve orientation.
The 360x800 search screenshot shows a large sexual ad fixed over the Artists/Authors controls, interrupting the core search task.
DOM inspection found four div role=dialog containers and zero <dialog> or popover elements; dismissal and modality are hand-wired.
The chapter template devotes nearly the entire viewport to the comic, with compact top and translucent bottom navigation.

checkOutcomes.method: layout metrics at 360x800 across four templates
checkOutcomes.evidence: Home, listing, detail and chapter all reported scrollWidth=clientWidth=360 and zero horizontal overflow with viewport metadata present.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence review: evidence/platform-probe.json, evidence/home-desktop.png, evidence/home-mobile.png
checkOutcomes.evidence: The CSS platform probe found no @container usage, even though cards are reused in materially different-width carousels and grids.
The active probe measured the Index dropdown toggle at 24x24 CSS px and the search input/button with outline-style none; other primary targets were 40-48px.
The search first viewport contains filters only, while the DOM text enumerates 1,643 tags before results; no result or direct path to results appears in the mobile screenshot.

checkOutcomes.method: manual representative navigation from detail action to chapter
checkOutcomes.evidence: Read Last links directly to Chapter 345, which loaded successfully with visible comic pages and labelled chapter navigation.

checkOutcomes.method: invalid-route exercise and form DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The invalid route shows a clear 404, plain-language message and GO HOME recovery link; forms use required constraints.
Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP at 3.9s (score 0.53); it identified the above-fold Queen Bee cover as loading=lazy without fetchpriority=high.
Mobile layout captures reported CLS 0 across templates; Lighthouse measured CLS 0.004 and all images have dimensions.

checkOutcomes.method: trace, layout long-task observers and Lighthouse TBT
checkOutcomes.evidence: Trace recorded one 63ms task and 13ms TBT; Lighthouse TBT was 10ms, with no sustained blocking on listing/chapter.
HAR and Lighthouse both identify axios.min.js as a high-priority parser-inserted render-blocking request; Lighthouse reports a 593ms longest dependency chain.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR byte breakdown and Lighthouse diagnostics
checkOutcomes.evidence: Only 35.9KiB of script transferred on home and 47.6KiB on chapter; no large duplicate/unused application bundle dominated the load.
DOM inspection found username, email and password fields with no associated label or aria-label, using placeholders alone; several submit buttons also expose no innerText in the DOM probe.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility audit and high-contrast computed styles
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 1.0 and the high-contrast probe retained visible text/control colors.
The homepage has two H1 elements (ManhwaRead and Home Page), several empty H2s, and the focused search controls report outline-style none.
Card titles, chapter labels and body UI remain readable at 360px without clipping or cramped horizontal wrapping.
The target probe measured the Index disclosure control at 24x24 CSS px, below the commonly usable 44px target, although narrow layouts otherwise reflow without overflow.
The errors-in-console audit passed and no uncaught exception was reported during the representative load.
The image primitive found five oversized homepage images; the 297x289 PNG logo is rendered at 40px and Lighthouse estimates 151KiB total image savings.
Lighthouse recorded three deprecation warnings, including Shared Storage and StorageType.persistent, from the Cloudflare challenge script.
All three templates expose descriptive, template-specific titles and meta descriptions.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM links, robots and viewport/layout probes
checkOutcomes.evidence: Navigation uses real href links, robots permits public content, and all tested templates include viewport metadata and fit 360px.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence review: evidence/lighthouse-home.json, evidence/home-recon.json, evidence/robots.txt
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse canonical audit scored 0 even though the rendered DOM resolves a canonical URL; this suggests malformed, conflicting or non-absolute source markup that should be normalised.
Detail and chapter pages include JSON-LD plus Open Graph title, description and image matching visible content.
The headers primitive confirmed HTTPS and HSTS but reported Content-Security-Policy absent.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR, tracker, cookie and secret scans
checkOutcomes.evidence: No known tracker domain or exposed secret was found; one secure HttpOnly first-party Cloudflare cookie was set, and third parties were primarily content/font/CDN origins.
The auth DOM contains username/password forms with no WebAuthn/passkey affordance and empty autocomplete attributes; no permission prompts fired on load.
The headers probe reports no CSP and does not reliably expose X-Content-Type-Options as present, while frame and referrer protections are configured.

checkOutcomes.method: discoverability raw-HTML comparison on three templates
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage, detail and chapter each had 100% rendered-content coverage in raw HTML and were not JS shells.

checkOutcomes.method: responsive screenshots, dialog DOM and task walkthrough
checkOutcomes.evidence: Menus, detail actions and reader controls remained within narrow viewports; the core detail-to-reader journey completed without a broken shell.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon and applicability judgement across representative paths
checkOutcomes.evidence: This content website is not presented as an installable app; offline installability is contextual, while no-JS content resilience was assessed separately.
checkOutcomes.reason: This content website is not presented as an installable app; offline installability is contextual, while no-JS content resilience was assessed separately.

checkOutcomes.evidence: A missing route renders a stable 404 with explanatory copy and a GO HOME action rather than a blank shell or spinner.
The document declares en-US; content order and mobile reflow remain coherent in the tested left-to-right locale.
Homepage cards render dates such as 14/01/2025 while html lang is en-US, a conflicting locale convention; no machine-readable time elements were found on the detail page.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon and applicability judgement across representative paths
checkOutcomes.evidence: Representative pages show publication dates but no events, appointments, recurrence or user-facing times that cross time zones.
checkOutcomes.reason: Representative pages show publication dates but no events, appointments, recurrence or user-facing times that cross time zones.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The ad overlays core controls, uses sexual clickbait and a dominant VIEW MORE action, while the user is trying to filter search results.
Login, registration and reset fields use native required constraints, preserving browser validation and preventing empty submission.
The DOM probe found empty autocomplete values on username, email, current password and new-password fields.
Only password login/register/reset controls are present; no passkey/WebAuthn path or reauthentication affordance was found.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence review: evidence/home-images.json, evidence/chapter-images.json, evidence/lighthouse-home.json
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 151KiB homepage image savings; the chapter loads JPEG pages through XHR/blob URLs and the image audit reports no responsive sources for 28 chapter images.
TBT was 10-13ms, script transfer stayed below 48KiB per sampled template, and no autoplay video/audio or known analytics tracker was found.
The homepage transfers 778,223 of 1,093,750 bytes from third parties; the sampled chapter transfers 807,474 of 1,104,616 bytes third-party, including 215KiB fonts.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon and applicability judgement across representative paths
checkOutcomes.evidence: No transactional or productivity capability is intended for agent invocation; public content is already fully available in raw HTML.
checkOutcomes.reason: No transactional or productivity capability is intended for agent invocation; public content is already fully available in raw HTML.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon and applicability judgement across representative paths
checkOutcomes.evidence: No summarisation or language-model feature is part of the reader experience, so on-device inference would not currently replace a server inference task.
checkOutcomes.reason: No summarisation or language-model feature is part of the reader experience, so on-device inference would not currently replace a server inference task.

checkOutcomes.method: baseline/post heap snapshots after 10 modal/sidebar cycles
checkOutcomes.evidence: After 10 open/close and sidebar toggle cycles, nodes fell 162,749 to 161,354 and self size fell 10,469,886 to 10,462,434 bytes after GC.
The homepage retained about 10.46MB self size after GC; this is proportionate to a media catalog and did not grow in the repeated interaction sample.
The post-interaction summary showed no growing Detached* constructor population and total nodes decreased after repeated UI cycles.

principleOutcomes.reason: This public content reader has no intended agent-invocable capability or on-device inference feature; raw content remains machine-readable.

paths.description: Homepage and discovery template; covers first impression, navigation, popular/new/latest content and global chrome.
Manhwa listing archetype; represents browse/catalog pages.
Queen Bee detail archetype; covers metadata and the primary Read First/Read Last journey.
Long-form chapter reader; covers the core reading task, long-scroll navigation and media delivery.
Search and advanced-filter flow for finding a title.
Representative invalid route to assess HTTP/navigation recovery.

findings.summary: An explicit ad obscures the advanced search controls on mobile.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 search screenshot shows a large sexual ad fixed over the Artists/Authors controls, interrupting the core search task.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the overlay ad from task surfaces or reserve a non-obscuring inline slot with an obvious, accessible dismiss control.

findings.summary: Search results are buried beneath an enormous advanced-filter surface and an overlay ad.
findings.evidence: The search first viewport contains filters only, while the DOM text enumerates 1,643 tags before results; no result or direct path to results appears in the mobile screenshot.
findings.suggestedFix: Show matching results immediately, collapse advanced filters behind a disclosure, and preserve a sticky result count/apply action.

findings.summary: The homepage LCP is outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP at 3.9s (score 0.53); it identified the above-fold Queen Bee cover as loading=lazy without fetchpriority=high.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not lazy-load the LCP cover, set fetchpriority=high for the selected hero/LCP image, and keep it discoverable in initial HTML.

findings.summary: Authentication form controls lack persistent accessible labels.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found username, email and password fields with no associated label or aria-label, using placeholders alone; several submit buttons also expose no innerText in the DOM probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit <label for> elements, correct autocomplete tokens and stable accessible button names.

findings.summary: The main document has no Content-Security-Policy.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirmed HTTPS and HSTS but reported Content-Security-Policy absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce- or hash-based CSP starting in Report-Only mode, then enforce a least-privilege script/style/connect/frame policy.

findings.summary: A parser-inserted Axios script blocks the critical path.
findings.evidence: HAR and Lighthouse both identify axios.min.js as a high-priority parser-inserted render-blocking request; Lighthouse reports a 593ms longest dependency chain.
findings.suggestedFix: Move non-critical scripts out of the critical path and load Axios with defer or replace it with fetch where feasible.

findings.summary: Account sign-in is password-only and lacks modern credential hints.
findings.evidence: The auth DOM contains username/password forms with no WebAuthn/passkey affordance and empty autocomplete attributes; no permission prompts fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey sign-in/registration with password fallback and set username/current-password/new-password autocomplete tokens.

findings.summary: The visual theme does not follow the system color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Light- and dark-preference screenshots are byte-identical (1,088,820 bytes) and both render the hard-coded dark theme; the page offers only a manual theme toggle.
findings.suggestedFix: Initialise the theme from prefers-color-scheme, declare color-scheme, and retain the manual override.

findings.summary: The 69,269px chapter reader gives no meaningful scroll progress.
findings.evidence: The chapter mobile layout is 69,269px tall, while the screenshot shows only a fixed chapter bar; the CSS probe found no scroll-state query or declarative progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an accessible scroll progress indicator using a declarative scroll-driven animation and keep chapter controls responsive to scroll state.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found View Transitions supported by the browser but no view-transition CSS usage; navigation is conventional abrupt document replacement.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document @view-transition for eligible navigations and same-document transitions for modal/filter state, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Authentication overlays are custom div dialogs instead of native dialog elements.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found four div role=dialog containers and zero <dialog> or popover elements; dismissal and modality are hand-wired.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> with showModal()/close() and platform focus containment, Escape handling and backdrop semantics.

findings.summary: Some controls have undersized targets or suppress visible focus styling.
findings.evidence: The active probe measured the Index dropdown toggle at 24x24 CSS px and the search input/button with outline-style none; other primary targets were 40-48px.
findings.suggestedFix: Expand every interactive hit area to at least 44x44 CSS px and provide a strong :focus-visible ring without removing the native outline unless replaced.

findings.summary: Heading and focus structure has avoidable defects.
findings.evidence: The homepage has two H1 elements (ManhwaRead and Home Page), several empty H2s, and the focused search controls report outline-style none.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one page-specific H1, remove empty headings, and add an obvious :focus-visible treatment that follows reading order.

findings.summary: Not all controls meet a robust target-size baseline.
findings.evidence: The target probe measured the Index disclosure control at 24x24 CSS px, below the commonly usable 44px target, although narrow layouts otherwise reflow without overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase the clickable disclosure area to at least 44x44 CSS px while retaining the compact icon.

findings.summary: Several images are materially oversized for their rendered dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found five oversized homepage images; the 297x289 PNG logo is rendered at 40px and Lighthouse estimates 151KiB total image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a correctly sized AVIF/WebP logo and tune responsive image candidates/compression for cover cards.

findings.summary: The homepage canonical signal fails Lighthouse validation.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse canonical audit scored 0 even though the rendered DOM resolves a canonical URL; this suggests malformed, conflicting or non-absolute source markup that should be normalised.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit one absolute self-referencing canonical URL in source HTML and verify it matches redirects and sitemap URLs.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The headers probe reports no CSP and does not reliably expose X-Content-Type-Options as present, while frame and referrer protections are configured.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP (including frame-ancestors), ensure X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff is emitted once and expand Permissions-Policy to the actual minimum capabilities.

findings.summary: Visible dates are fixed-format strings rather than locale-aware output.
findings.evidence: Homepage cards render dates such as 14/01/2025 while html lang is en-US, a conflicting locale convention; no machine-readable time elements were found on the detail page.
findings.suggestedFix: Render dates with Intl.DateTimeFormat for the active locale and use <time datetime> with unambiguous stored values.

findings.summary: The mobile search journey uses an obstructive promotional ad pattern.
findings.evidence: The ad overlays core controls, uses sexual clickbait and a dominant VIEW MORE action, while the user is trying to filter search results.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep promotions clearly labelled, non-obstructive and visually subordinate to the user-initiated task.

findings.summary: Sign-in, registration and reset fields omit autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found empty autocomplete values on username, email, current password and new-password fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply username, email, current-password and new-password autocomplete tokens to the corresponding fields.

findings.summary: The account flow does not offer phishing-resistant authentication.
findings.evidence: Only password login/register/reset controls are present; no passkey/WebAuthn path or reauthentication affordance was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkeys as the preferred account path, retain recoverable fallback, and clearly explain account state and reversal.

findings.summary: Image delivery leaves meaningful avoidable byte savings.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 151KiB homepage image savings; the chapter loads JPEG pages through XHR/blob URLs and the image audit reports no responsive sources for 28 chapter images.
findings.suggestedFix: Right-size and recompress covers/logo, and deliver chapter pages with responsive modern image candidates while preserving progressive loading.

findings.summary: Third-party media and fonts dominate transferred bytes.
findings.evidence: The homepage transfers 778,223 of 1,093,750 bytes from third parties; the sampled chapter transfers 807,474 of 1,104,616 bytes third-party, including 215KiB fonts.
findings.suggestedFix: Self-host/subset fonts, reduce Font Awesome payload, cache content-CDN assets aggressively and defer below-fold media requests.

findings.summary: Reusable cards and controls rely on viewport styling rather than container queries.
findings.evidence: The CSS platform probe found no @container usage, even though cards are reused in materially different-width carousels and grids.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card/list components containment and adapt them with size container queries where their parent width, not viewport width, governs layout.

findings.summary: A Cloudflare challenge script triggers deprecated API warnings.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse recorded three deprecation warnings, including Shared Storage and StorageType.persistent, from the Cloudflare challenge script.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or reconfigure the challenge integration so it no longer ships deprecated API paths to ordinary page loads.
